newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila o/night rates ease, banks square positions.
newsitem.headline: Manila o/night rates ease, banks square positions.

text.p: Philippine interbank call loan rates eased on Tuesday after more than a week of tightness.
The average rate fell to 13.9375 from 14.5625 percent after banks were able to square their positions, traders said.
"Most of the borrowers had become square," said a trader.
"Banks used several strategies to correct their positions. They held off from investment in government securities and dollars," another trader said.
Done rates ranged from 15.5 to 11.75 percent, with 36 lenders and 28 borrowers. Volume thinned to 21.786 billion from 23.618 billion pesos.
Since last week, rates had jumped due to reserve covering for the long weekend during the last week of October.

With the easing of rates, one trader said, the Central Bank may soon drop its overnight lending rate. Last Wednesday, the Central Bank raised its overnight lending to 15 from 13 percent in view of the tightness in the market.
The secondary market for T-bills continued to see lacklustre trading, traders said.
"It's still not moving. Some banks were even quoting off-market rates so that their T-bills could be bought. But no one reacted," a dealer said.
Banks opted to stay liquid, traders said.

Moreover, attention was on the auction of two-year Treasury notes later in the day which is expected to yield a rate of 13.75 percent, dealers said. Three-month bill was quoted an offer rate from 11.625 to 11.90; the six months at 12.0 to 12.6; and the one year at 12.6 to 13.0. - LILIAN KARUNUNGAN (632) 841-8937
